redesigned_cot:
APPROACH CHOSEN (best R-vs-oracle tradeoff of three considered): "Constraint-narrowed local lookup over a fixed dictionary." REJECTED ALT-A = keep full 77-word scan but reformat the verdict (still R7-heavy, 3000+ tokens, the scan adds no oracle). REJECTED ALT-B = drop unknown-letter handling entirely / box from examples only (BREAKS oracle on the 63% hard path). CHOSEN keeps EXACT oracle (200/200 verified) while cutting completion to median 778 / max 1007 tokens by deleting only the non-load-bearing scan chaff and converting the bare selection into a local copy. Every committed token is a copy of a string printed earlier in the SAME trace.

RIGID SKELETON (one helper formats every line byte-identically; same for easy and hard paths; only slot values differ):

Line 1 (fixed): "We need to find the substitution cipher mapping from the examples, then decrypt the question."

SECTION 1 — EXAMPLE ALIGNMENT (anchor + local-derive source for the map). Header (fixed): "Examples (cipher -> plain), aligned letter by letter:". Then for each example, blank line, then "[<cipher_sentence>] -> [<plain_sentence>]" (verbatim restatement = R2 anchor), then ONE LINE PER LETTER in fixed template "<cipher_char> -> <plain_char>" covering every letter of every word in printed order (R3 one-fact-per-line). The plain_char is copied from the bracket line directly above (regime-1 copy).

SECTION 2 — MAPPING TABLE (the master anchor, R2). Blank line, header (fixed): "Mapping so far:". Then EXACTLY 26 lines, one per a..z in alphabetical order, template "<letter> -> <plain or ?>". This is the single copy source consumed by every decrypt step. (Keep it complete with '?' rows — never slim; restatement HELPS R.)

SECTION 3 — DECRYPT QUESTION, word by word. Blank line, header (fixed): "Decrypting the question: <question_sentence>" (verbatim restatement). For EACH question word, in order:
  - blank line, then "word: <cipher_word>" (anchor of the operand).
  - ONE LINE PER LETTER, template "<cipher_char> -> <plain_or_?>", each plain copied from the 26-line Mapping table (short, fixed key = the letter). This re-reads the operand locally.
  - then "= <assembled_word>" on its own line: a pure left-to-right copy of the plain chars just printed (when all known). 
  - IF the word has unknown letters (contains ?): instead of a bare pick, emit this rigid LOCAL-NARROWING block:
      "pattern: <partial>"  (e.g. "pattern: ?right" — copied from the per-letter lines just above)
      "letters still unused for plain: <space-joined list of plain letters not yet a value in the map>"  (anchor for the bijectivity constraint, copied conceptually from the '?' rows of the table)
      "the only vocabulary word of length <N> matching pattern <partial> with unused letters in the blanks is <word>"  (the surviving-unique candidate; <word> is a regime-2 lookup over the FIXED 77-word dict, uniquely keyed by the printed pattern — proven unique 455/455 single-unknown, 56/56 after the unused-letter filter)
      "= <word>"  (copy of the word just named)
      then ONE LINE PER newly-resolved letter, template "new mapping: <cipher_char> -> <plain_char>" (copied char-aligned from <word> vs <cipher_word>), so downstream words read these from here too.

SECTION 4 — ANSWER ASSEMBLY (R6 self-consistent box). Blank line, then "Answer: <space-join of every '= <word>' result, in order>". The completion suffix (pinned, identical to corpus.py): the box is "\\boxed{<that exact same join>}". Box is a character-for-character copy of the assembled words (verified 0/300 mismatch).

KEY R MOVES vs current: (1) DELETE the 77-row-per-word scan loop entirely (non-load-bearing; oracle identical). (2) REPLACE 'Best match: [X]' with the 3-line LOCAL pattern->unique-word block whose decisive evidence (pattern + unused letters) sits on the two lines immediately above the named word — converts an R4 bare selection into a regime-2 copy keyed by a printed string. (3) Re-emit each operand close to its consume site (word: line right above its per-letter copies) shrinking retrieval span (R3/M3). (4) One byte-identical template per line via a single formatter; full a..z table always present (R5). (5) Both easy and hard paths now share the identical surface shape (the unknown block is the only optional element and it is guarded by the always-present "pattern:" literal cue), killing the multimodal-continuation risk. Length drops 4x (median 778, max 1007 comp tokens) giving huge cap margin.
oracle_preservation_argument: The redesigned CoT computes the answer by EXACTLY the same deterministic procedure as the current reasoner, only deleting display chaff (the 77-word scan rows) and reformatting the selection — it does not change WHICH word is chosen. Proof points, all run offline: (1) Re-implemented the redesigned derivation (build c2p from examples letter-by-letter; decrypt via c2p; for unknown words take the constraint-filtered candidate exactly as cipher.py lines 257-347 do: _candidate_words_for_partial + reject unknowns mapping to already-used plain letters + prefer wonderland word + take first) and compared its final string to the CURRENT reasoner's extract_answer(reasoning_cipher(p)) on 200 random cipher problems: 200/200 IDENTICAL, 0 mismatch, 0 current-None. (2) The 'Best match' is provably forced-unique: after the bijectivity/unused-letter filter exactly one candidate survives on 56/56 sampled unknown question-words, so removing the visible 77-word scan cannot change the result — the scan is pure display, the filter is the decider and the filter is unchanged. (3) The fixed 77-word vocabulary makes every single-unknown pattern unique (455/455), and the multi-unknown cases (2-4 unknowns, 52 sampled) all resolve to one word after adding the unused-letter constraint (already part of the preserved filter). (4) The box is a literal copy of the assembled per-word results (box == ' '.join(per-word) on 300/300). Therefore the grader-correct answer is reproduced, and since corpus.py boxes the CoT's own extracted answer, self-consistency holds.
offline_validation: Run these four checks (all green in this session; rerun after implementing render): (A) ORACLE-EQUALITY: for >=200 random cipher problems assert redesigned_answer(p) == extract_answer(reasoning_cipher(p)); require 0 mismatch / 0 None. (B) FORCED-UNIQUE: for every unknown question-word assert the post-filter candidate set (wonderland-preferred, then unused-letter constraint) has size exactly 1 (got 56/56). (C) TEMPLATE UNIFORMITY: render the redesigned CoT for a sample, diff several traces and assert only literal slot values differ (same headers/order/separators), assert the unknown block always begins with the literal cue 'pattern:', and assert the trace contains no substring matching the global-rule grep set ('the rule is','pattern is X','the shift is','secret is','the cipher is'). (D) UNDER-CAP + BOX-CONSISTENCY: tokenize completion '{cot}\\n</think>\\n\\boxed{{{ans}}}<|im_end|>' with src/tokenizer.json over >=200 problems, assert max comp_ids <= GEN_LIMIT (7680) with margin (got max 1007), and assert the boxed string == ' '.join of the per-word '= <word>' results char-for-char (got 0/300 mismatch).

verdict_fixes.counterexample: none found after honest effort. I constructed a real structural defect (2+ blank-position collision classes that survive the unused-letter filter: '?oo?'->{book,door}, '??ight'->{bright,knight}, 'g??den'->{garden,golden}, '?a?'->{cat,map}; exhaustive scan of the fixed 77-word vocab found 8 such 2-blank, 41 3-blank, 71 4-blank collision signatures). I built a synthetic in-distribution problem (secret cipher with o->o known, plain letters b,d,r,k kept unused, question cipher word 'koop' for gold 'door') and confirmed the redesigned CoT boxes 'book' (WRONG). HOWEVER this is NOT a redesign regression: the CURRENT reasoner boxes 'book' on the identical input (verified: reasoner box == redesign box == 'book', both wrong, because both share the sorted-first tie-break wonderland_remaining[0] after the unused-letter filter leaves {book,door}). And this configuration NEVER occurs in real data: on all 1576 train + 315 holdout cipher problems the current reasoner matches gold 1891/1891, and the redesign matches the reasoner 1891/1891 (0 None, 0 brace, 0 gold-mismatch). The forced-unique claim verified stronger than proposed: 1310/1310 real unknown words yield exactly one wonderland candidate even under the weaker literal filter (length+known-pos+unused-blank, dropping repeat-pattern), and 0/384 multi-unknown-word problems are order-ambiguous. The 2-blank collision risk is a pre-existing shared limitation, not introduced by removing the scan/selection.
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: No fix required for oracle preservation: the redesign reproduces the current reasoner's answer byte-for-byte on 1891/1891 real problems (train+holdout), returns None 0 times, and is provably forced-unique on every real unknown word. Optional hardening (would improve BOTH reasoner and redesign on the synthetic 2+blank-collision tail, which is absent from real data): when the unused-letter filter leaves >1 candidate, add a deterministic disambiguation rule and PRINT the decisive evidence inline — e.g. emit each surviving candidate's required new-mapping triples and reject any candidate that would map an unknown cipher letter to a plain letter already forced elsewhere, then if still tied keep the rigid 'lowest sorted candidate' tie-break but show the full surviving set on the line directly above the verdict (so the model copies an exhibited choice rather than inferring it). This stays R4-compliant (mechanical, evidence-adjacent) and R1-local. It changes no real-data answer (0/1891), so it is oracle-neutral on the measured distribution.

verdict_fixes.counterexample: none found after honest effort. Searched the full 1576-problem corpus for the worst case: the ambiguous multi-blank pattern '?oo?' (matches both 'book' and 'door'). In the real instance 'hffk' (answer 'cat imagines book'), the printed 'unused plain letters: b j k x z' line deterministically rejects 'door' (needs 'd', already mapped/not unused) and forces 'book' (needs 'b','k', both unused). No instance requires a value or rule that is absent from the printed page; no instance is multimodal on the printed key; no instance boxes a wrong answer (redesigned == current-reasoner-box == ground-truth, 400/400 sampled, answer-mismatch 0/1576 on full render).
verdict_fixes.fix_if_needed: Implement as designed; it is the correct R-maximizing redesign for cipher. Two cheap hardening tweaks, neither blocking: (1) R8 drill — ship an empty-<think> augmenter that drills 'pattern <partial> + unused <letters> -> <unique word>' over the fixed 77-word vocab in the IDENTICAL surface format, to widen the argmax margin on the single regime-2 lookup slot (the one non-copy token, hence the highest-residual-entropy slot in the trace). (2) R5 guard — give the known-word terminator an always-present literal cue symmetric to 'pattern:' (e.g. always emit a 'status:' line: 'status: all known' vs 'status: has unknown') so the branch cue is an explicit printed literal rather than relying on the model inferring branch from the presence of '?'. Both are oracle-neutral (verified: deleting the 77-row scan and reformatting selection leaves the chosen word identical, 400/400). Do NOT add the cipher repeat-pattern to the 'unique word' justification — it is never needed (0/1453) and would add tokens/entropy. Keep the full 26-line a..z mapping table (anchor; never slim). Run the four offline checks (oracle-equality, forced-unique==1, template-uniformity+grep-clean, under-cap+box-consistency) after rendering — all green this session: oracle 400/400, forced-unique 1453/1453, grep clean, max 1065 tokens, box-consistency 1576/1576.
rubric_violations: MINOR/RESIDUAL (not a violation, design-inherent): the line 'the only vocabulary word ... is <word>' emits a word that is NOT a verbatim copy of any earlier token — it is produced from the fixed 77-word vocab. I verified this is benign regime-2, NOT the R-collapsing regime-3: across ALL 1576 corpus problems / 1453 unknown-word resolutions, the PRINTED key (pattern + 'unused letters' line) forces a UNIQUE word 1453/1453 (1422 by pattern alone; all 31 ambiguous multi-blank cases e.g. ?oo?->book resolved by the printed unused-letters constraint; 0 need the un-printed cipher repeat-pattern). The conditional p(word|printed key) is non-multimodal corpus-wide (0/1453 same-key->different-gold), so greedy argmax cannot flip. This is the maximum achievable; the word genuinely isn't on the page pre-lookup, so it cannot be a pure copy. R4 is correctly converted from bare-selection to printed-evidence-keyed lookup.

MINOR R5 (template branching, deterministic): per word the trace branches between '= <word>' (known) and the 'pattern:' unknown block. I confirmed the branch is decided by a LOCAL printed cue (presence of '<c> -> ?' in the per-letter lines just above), so the continuation after the identical 'word:'-block prefix is deterministic from the page, not multimodal. Acceptable, but worth a fixed always-present literal guard as the audit recommends.
